title: Motion designs: eight more repos from the owner's second Google Doc
source: The owner's Google Doc 'Motion designs' (id 1BIonbd5ESm0b4EpSe9VZp38h77M0adWOriGOYFvT3ZQ), read from Drive on 2026-10-11 (GSAP and lottie-web in it are covered in 2026-10-11). Dossiers by `python -m faceless intake`; READMEs were mostly short, so these judgments rest on stated purpose, licence files and what the studio already runs.

items.name: claude-motion-design (howseen-ai)
items.why: MIT. A Claude Code skill for motion videos in pure code with HTML, Playwright and ffmpeg: the same method the studio already runs (HyperFrames is HTML plus headless Chrome plus ffmpeg), and the same loop the JavaScript Claude video teaches (storyboard first, contact sheet, fix, re-render). Read from its README only.
items.steal: Its storyboard-before-code step and contact-sheet check, as a gate for new drawn scenes.
items.owner: Read it once before building the next ledger scene kinds; do not install it.

items.name: hyperframes-motion-reel-skill (Sunwood-ai-labs)
items.why: MIT. A skill for motion reels on HyperFrames, which is our renderer. Closest match to the stack, so the likeliest source of scene patterns that already respect HyperFrames' seek rules.
items.steal: Reel structures and scene patterns for new card kinds.
items.owner: Read its patterns when adding a card kind; copy ideas, not files.

items.name: motion-graphics-skills (charlie947)
items.why: MIT. A set of motion-graphics skills; the README gave the dossier little to judge, so it is not wired in. Our own skills (faceless-hyperframes, faceless-ledger) already cover the loop.
items.steal: Prompts for specific effects, if one is missing.
items.owner: Skim when a scene needs an effect we lack.

items.name: claude-motion (whaleyxbt)
items.why: MIT, but the dossier found nothing about what it does. The same author's patchright-enhanced is already rejected in the registry (anti-detection scraping), which is no reason to reject this one, but it is a reason not to install it unread.
items.owner: Read the README by hand before any use.

items.name: claude-remotion-skill (haidrrrry)
items.why: MIT skill for Remotion. We render with HyperFrames; a Remotion skill would pull in a second renderer and a Node/React build for no gain.

items.name: Remotion (remotion-dev/remotion)
items.why: React video renderer. The intake tool read the licence file as MIT, but Remotion's own terms are a source-available licence that asks companies above a small size to buy one; verify by hand before ever relying on it. It duplicates HyperFrames (HTML to MP4 locally, Apache-2.0, already pinned and hash-checked). Moves the registry's earlier PARK to KILL.
items.steal: Its idea of a video as a function of the frame number, which the drawn series already uses.

items.name: klik-anim-skill-creation (t3knobox)
items.why: No licence file found and no README text the dossier could judge; unverified.
items.owner: Check the licence and README by hand before using any of it.

items.name: awesome-motion-design-agent-skills (frankxai)
items.why: A curated list (CC0 by its badge; the licence file text was not recognised, so check). Useful as a reading list, not a dependency.
items.steal: Names of other skills worth a look.
items.owner: Browse it when looking for a specific technique.
